name: Adrafinil

lead: Adrafinil is converted by the liver into modafinil, so users take it as a non-prescription route to the same wakefulness for study and work. It was sold in France as Olmifon from the mid-1980s for sleepiness and inattention in older adults until 2011.
Its effects are attributed to modafinil, which acts on the dopamine transporter. Human clinical research is thin, and no trial has tested it for appearance outcomes.

paras: It is sold as a supplement or research chemical in some markets and taken orally for alertness and productivity.
Human safety data are limited. It is not approved for any use in the US and is listed as a stimulant in doping control.

angle.text: Adrafinil is turned into modafinil in the body, so users take it for alertness and a steadier work and study routine without a prescription. It was sold in France for vigilance in older adults.

lead: Adrafinil is a wakefulness-promoting compound that the body converts to modafinil. According to Grokipedia, it was developed by Laboratoire Lafon in France, marketed there as Olmifon from the mid-1980s for vigilance problems in older adults, and withdrawn by its manufacturer in 2011 [1].

Because it is a precursor of modafinil, its effects are attributed to that metabolite, which acts on the dopamine transporter [1][2]. Adrafinil is not approved by the US Food and Drug Administration for any use and is sold outside prescription channels in some markets as a supplement or research chemical, per Grokipedia [1]. It is also on doping-control lists as a stimulant, and chemists have published methods to detect it [3][4].

No published human trial has tested adrafinil for any appearance outcome. The sources reviewed contain no looksmaxxing forum material about it, so its place in appearance culture is not documented here beyond its relation to modafinil.
infobox: Withdrawn in France in 2011, per Grokipedia [1]

paras: Grokipedia describes adrafinil as metabolised in the liver to modafinil, with modafinil responsible for the central effects [1]. A 2020 review covering modafinil pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics discusses clinical and forensic aspects of the drug and its parent compounds [2]. Analytical chemistry papers have separated adrafinil from modafinil by chromatography and developed fluorescent sensors to detect adrafinil, which is described as a banned performance-enhancing drug [4][5].

Grokipedia places adrafinil's development in the 1970s at Laboratoire Lafon, with French marketing authorisation around 1985 for vigilance disorders in the elderly, early experimental use in narcolepsy, and a voluntary market withdrawal in 2011 [1]. A 2018 history article describes the discovery of modafinil and its early European use [6].

No studies of adrafinil in healthy people for appearance outcomes were found. Published research is mostly preclinical: behavioural studies in aged dogs examined adrafinil's activating effects, compared it with propentofylline and nicergoline, and the canine ageing model has been used to evaluate cognition-enhancing drugs [7][8][9]. Rodent studies used adrafinil as one of several stimulants in an anxiety test procedure [10]. Grokipedia says human clinical evidence is limited and runs mainly through the modafinil metabolite [1].

Adrafinil appears in doping literature as a stimulant that is legal in some settings and prohibited in sport, with reviews of stimulant prevalence in athletes and published detection methods [3][4]. Grokipedia describes it as unregulated in the US as a research chemical or supplement [1]. This wiki does not document sourcing.
